items.title: Cabinet approves 5.3% minimum wage rise for 2027
items.body: The cabinet approved a 5.3% rise in the SMI (minimum wage) for 2027 on November 17. It sets pay at €1,286 a month in 14 payments, with the IRPF (personal income tax) exemption unchanged.

items.title: Retirement age reaches 67 in January 2027
items.body: Under the 2013 pension reform, the standard retirement age reaches 67 on January 1, 2027. Workers can still retire at 65 with at least 38 years and six months of contributions. The change aims to keep Social Security sustainable as the population ages.

items.title: PP and PSOE set out income tax pledges
items.body: Ahead of the November 29 election, PP proposes inflation-adjusted IRPF brackets and state tax cuts of 100%, 75%, 50%, and 25% over the first four filing years for ages 18–35. PSOE proposes a 10% rent deduction for incomes below €33,007.20. Neither party has published detailed costings; these are campaign pledges, not law.

items.title: Canary Islands arrivals strain migrant reception centres
items.body: Spain recorded 44,238 irregular entries through November 15, up from 31,742 a year earlier, excluding the mass Ceuta crossing. Canary Islands arrivals rose 65.9% to 24,364. The islands host 3,313 unaccompanied migrant minors against an ordinary capacity of 782 places.

items.title: Cabinet approves pay transparency rules and higher fines
items.body: The cabinet approved a pay-transparency decree-law on November 17; parliament's standing committee must still validate it. To cut the gender pay gap, it would require starting pay in job adverts, bar salary-history questions, and raise the maximum fine for withholding essential contract information from €750 to €7,500.

items.title: Public-sector pay rise goes before cabinet
items.body: A planned 4.5% public-sector pay rise goes before the cabinet on November 17. It would apply from January 1, 2027, for more than three million workers. An extra 0.5% would bring the total to 5% if final December inflation reaches at least 1.5%.

items.title: Five Spanish olive oils reach global top 10
items.body: Evooleum's top 10 includes Oleum Hispania Nature Premium Pajarera (96 points), Parqueoliva Serie Oro (96), Dehesa El Molinillo Coratina (95), El Santuario de Mágina Selección Temprana (95), and Rincón de la Subbética (94). Spain has 68 of the guide's top 100 oils.

items.title: November 17 rail strike disrupts services across Spain
items.body: A 24-hour rail strike on November 17 has cancelled 90 of 312 planned high-speed departures. Renfe says Madrid and Catalonia commuter trains are running below minimum service levels. Unions demand more staff and safety improvements after two rail accidents, alleging the government failed to honour earlier agreements.

items.title: Intelligence centre finds no proof Morocco orchestrated Ceuta crossing
items.body: Spain's intelligence centre, CNI, told a judge it found no evidence that Morocco organised July's mass crossing into Ceuta, involving more than 80,000 people. It points instead to viral social media calls, misleading reports about a court ruling, weather, and reduced border surveillance.

items.title: Election rivals debate on November 19
items.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo debate on November 19 at 22.00, ahead of the November 29 election. Housing, taxes, public services, corruption, and migration are on the agenda. Viewers can watch on La 1, Canal 24 horas, RTVE Play, Antena 3, and La Sexta.

items.title: Butane cylinders rise to €19.55 from November 17
items.body: The regulated maximum price of a 12.5 kg butane cylinder rises 3.95% to €19.55 on November 17, under a price update published in the BOE (official state gazette). Higher raw material and freight costs, plus a weaker euro, drove the rise. A cap holds the maximum at €19.55 until June 2027.

items.title: Lung cancer becomes women's leading cancer killer
items.body: Lung cancer caused 6,691 deaths among women in Spain in 2024, overtaking breast cancer's 6,563 for the first time. Smoking causes 85% of lung cancer cases. Catalonia and Castilla-La Mancha have announced screening programmes for 2027, while specialists call for equal access nationwide.

items.title: Italian court orders oversight of Revolut branch
items.body: A Milan court placed Revolut's Italian branch under judicial administration for one year over alleged anti-money-laundering failures linked to €76.5 million in suspicious transfers. Administrators will supervise and fix control systems. The order leaves normal customer operations unchanged.
